chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Musa ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about statues that are on the carpet with two eyes, while you are praying. He said: 'If it has one eye, there is no harm (with it), and if it has two eyes, there is no (prayer validity).'
ai.seo_question: Does the presence of a statue with eyes on the prayer carpet invalidate salat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a nuanced criterion for *ghurur* (distraction) in prayer based on the anthropomorphic features of statues, specifically distinguishing between one-eyed and two-eyed figures. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on minimizing visual distractions that may divert the worshipper’s heart from the presence of God, with two eyes symbolizing a more complete, lifelike presence that competes for attention. The distinction highlights the juristic principle that prayer validity depends on the degree of cognitive engagement with the idolatrous image rather than its mere existence.
